paragraphs: Tensor completion concerns filling in missing entries of a multidimensional array using low-rank structure. The paper examines an approach based on latent trace norm regularization. Existing methods of this kind often favor a sparse combination of component tensors, meaning that relatively few components contribute to the recovered result.

The authors introduce a variant of that regularizer designed to support a non-sparse combination. They then develop a dual formulation of the completion problem and characterize its solution space. Their analysis reveals a factorization of the optimal solution, placing it on a Cartesian product of Riemannian manifolds: a collection of spaces with structured geometry.

That geometric characterization supplies a route to computation. The authors use Riemannian optimization to construct a computationally efficient trust region algorithm suited to the solution space. Experiments on real-world datasets across several applications illustrate its effectiveness. The contribution therefore connects a different preference about how tensor components combine with a mathematical formulation and an algorithm for finding the resulting completion.
neurips-2018-a-dual-framework-for-low-ra.tldr: A modified tensor regularizer and geometric dual formulation enable efficient completion using non-sparse combinations of component tensors.

paragraphs: Dynamical latent variable models describe observations through hidden quantities that evolve over time. Filtering estimates those hidden quantities using only information available up to the current moment. The paper develops a general variational inference method for this setting, keeping future variables outside the information used for each inference step.

The proposed variational filtering EM algorithm follows from the variational objective under this information restriction. It performs an optimization procedure at every time step. This gives a common starting point for inference across dynamical models: determine the current hidden-state approximation by optimizing an objective that respects what is presently known.

To make that repeated optimization computationally efficient, the authors implement it with an iterative amortized inference model. A learned inference procedure carries out the successive updates, producing the method they call amortized variational filtering. Experiments show improved inference performance across several recent deep dynamical latent variable models. These findings support the usefulness of a shared inference approach across those models while retaining the past-and-present information requirement central to filtering.
neurips-2018-a-general-method-for-amorti.tldr: Amortized variational filtering uses learned iterative inference to efficiently estimate evolving hidden states from past and present information.

paragraphs: Adversarial generation has worked well for real-valued data, but text presents an obstacle because its outputs are discrete. This paper changes the training objective for text-generating adversarial networks. Its central proposal is to compare distributions of sentence features, giving training a measure of disagreement between real and generated language.

The authors introduce feature-mover's distance, a metric inspired by optimal transport, to match these latent feature distributions. The comparison happens in a representation of sentences rather than through the standard GAN objective. They describe the resulting critic as highly discriminative and the objective as easy to optimize, addressing unstable training and mode collapse, where generation loses variety.

Experiments cover unconditional text generation, style transfer using non-parallel text, and unsupervised cipher cracking. The proposed model achieves superior performance in the reported evaluations. The breadth of those tasks matters because they place different demands on language generation and transformation. Together, the results support the authors' claim that feature-distribution matching is an effective and broadly applicable training approach across the tasks studied.
neurips-2018-adversarial-text-generation.tldr: Feature-mover's distance improves adversarial text generation by matching real and generated sentence-feature distributions through an optimal-transport-inspired objective.

paragraphs: In goal-oriented dialog, questions serve a practical purpose: their answers should help the questioner identify an appropriate action. Learning a capable questioner is difficult when it requires learning whole sequences of sentences. This paper proposes choosing questions by explicitly reasoning about what an answerer is likely to say.

The method, Answerer in Questioner's Mind, equips the questioner with an approximate probabilistic model of the answerer. For a possible question, it considers candidate intentions and possible responses, then calculates the information gain. This makes question selection depend on how much an answer could clarify the intention the questioner is trying to identify.

The authors evaluate the framework on MNIST Counting Dialog and GuessWhat?!, two goal-oriented visual dialog tasks. It outperforms the comparison algorithms by a large margin in their experiments. These findings support the usefulness of explicitly modeling the conversational partner and evaluating the informativeness of questions. The approximate answerer model is central to the approach: it supplies the predictions on which both questioning and inference rely.
neurips-2018-answerer-in-questioner-s-mi.tldr: AQM selects informative visual-dialog questions by predicting possible answers with an approximate model of the answerer.

paragraphs: COLA addresses training linear classification and regression models when data resides across many user devices. Learning must happen on those devices, and communication takes place over an arbitrary network without a central coordinator. This setting makes coordination and communication part of the learning problem rather than assuming that training data can be pooled.

The paper proposes a decentralized training algorithm with strong theoretical guarantees and reports superior practical performance. Its framework targets communication efficiency and scalability, so the organization of computation across devices is a central concern. It also supports elasticity and resilience to changing data, accommodating a learning environment whose participating resources and information can evolve.

The framework further allows unreliable devices and differences between participating devices. These properties matter because a decentralized system must operate with more variation than a uniformly managed collection of machines. The stated contribution combines these practical capabilities with theoretical guarantees for linear learning. Data ownership and privacy motivate the setting, while the concrete result concerns training across distributed devices without requiring a central coordinator.
neurips-2018-cola-decentralized-linear-l.tldr: COLA trains linear models across decentralized devices without a central coordinator while addressing communication, scalability, and device variability.

paragraphs: Community inference seeks hidden groups in a network. This paper studies a setting with two sources of evidence: a sparse graph and high-dimensional attributes attached to its nodes. Both sources are correlated with the same underlying communities, raising the question of what can be inferred when their information is considered together.

The authors provide an information-theoretically tight analysis of this problem. Such an analysis concerns the information available for inference, rather than only the behavior of a particular heuristic. The work connects theoretical progress on graph-only community detection with empirical approaches that have combined graph connections and node attributes in diverse ways.

A consequence of the tight analysis is that combining the information sources is necessary in the information-theoretic sense captured by the model. This gives a formal basis for joint use of relationships and attributes. The stated scope of the analysis includes networks with large degrees and a Gaussian version of the model. Those conditions locate the result: the paper establishes sharp theoretical conclusions within these settings.
neurips-2018-contextual-stochastic-block.tldr: A tight theoretical analysis explains why community inference can require jointly using graph connections and node attributes.

paragraphs: Cooperative neural networks use several jointly trained networks to learn hidden representations that respect a supplied independence structure. That structure expresses prior knowledge about how variables relate. The aim is to bring such domain knowledge into neural learning while retaining more flexibility than traditional graphical models built from exponential-family distributions.

The framework occupies a middle ground between those graphical models and conventional deep networks or variational autoencoders. It incorporates more explicit prior structure than the latter, and the authors describe it as general enough to use the independence structure of any graphical model. Their concrete example transfers the structure of Latent Dirichlet Allocation into a model called CoNN-sLDA.

The paper evaluates CoNN-sLDA on supervised text classification. On the challenging MultiSent dataset, it reports a 23 percent reduction in error relative to the state of the art. This empirical result shows that the intended benefit of prior independence structure can appear in practical classification performance. It supports the demonstrated text-model construction while illustrating the broader framework's strategy of combining structured assumptions with flexible neural representations.
neurips-2018-cooperative-neural-networks.tldr: CoNN incorporates graphical-model independence structure into cooperating neural networks, with improved results in a supervised text-classification example.

paragraphs: Regulating a data center involves controlling temperatures and airflow in a physical environment where mistakes can be expensive. The paper studies reinforcement learning for this task inside a large-scale data center. Its motivation is practical: unexpected events, limited data, and costly failures can complicate the deployment of learning-based control.

The authors adopt a data-driven, model-based approach. This places a model within the control strategy and uses experience from the system to support learning. The agent starts with little prior knowledge, making the amount of exploration needed especially relevant. The reported demonstration shows that it can effectively and safely regulate conditions on a server floor after only a few hours of exploration.

The agent also improves operational efficiency relative to the existing PID controllers. These findings connect learning speed, operational control, and efficiency within the same deployment. Their significance is the demonstrated use of reinforcement learning in a real physical system under the practical constraints highlighted by the authors. The safety and efficiency claims describe the reported data-center application.
neurips-2018-data-center-cooling-using-m.tldr: A model-based reinforcement-learning controller learns to regulate a data-center server floor safely and efficiently after a few hours of exploration.

paragraphs: Bayesian inference represents conclusions as posterior beliefs, so the uncertainty introduced by a privacy mechanism matters to the result. This paper addresses private inference for exponential-family models. Its central concern is accounting for privacy noise within the inference procedure, so that the reported beliefs reflect that additional source of uncertainty.

The authors present what they describe as the first method in this setting to account properly for noise introduced by the privacy mechanism. The method operates on sufficient statistics rather than individual data records. These statistics provide the summaries used for inference in the model, and working with them is the stated reason for the method's efficiency.

The main finding is properly calibrated posterior beliefs in the non-asymptotic data regime, where the result does not depend on an effectively unlimited amount of data. That distinction matters because noise from privacy protection remains part of the evidence available for inference. The contribution ties efficient summary-based computation to uncertainty accounting, with exponential families defining the class of models considered.
neurips-2018-differentially-private-baye.tldr: The method accounts for privacy noise in exponential-family Bayesian inference to produce calibrated posterior beliefs with finite data.

paragraphs: Large training datasets can be difficult to assemble when practical, ethical, or legal concerns complicate sharing records across sites. The paper considers situations where sharing derived datasets or predictive models may face fewer restrictions. Its goal is to combine learning from separate datasets through the networks trained on them.

Distributed weight consolidation, or DWC, consolidates the weights of independently trained neural networks. The authors frame it as a continual learning method, addressing the sequential training requirement of existing approaches discussed in the abstract. The key organizational change is that networks trained separately on independent datasets become the inputs to consolidation.

The evaluation uses brain segmentation with dilated convolutional networks trained on structural MRI datasets from different sites. Compared with an ensemble baseline, DWC improves performance on test sets from those sites while maintaining generalization on a very large, completely independent multi-site dataset. These results distinguish improved performance within the participating sites from preserved performance on independent data, providing evidence for model consolidation in this case study.
neurips-2018-distributed-weight-consolid.tldr: DWC combines independently trained networks, improving site-specific brain segmentation while maintaining generalization on an independent multi-site dataset.

paragraphs: The paper studies smooth nonconvex optimization when solutions must remain inside a convex set. Its focus is escaping saddle points and reaching a second-order stationary point, where both gradient and curvature conditions are satisfied to specified tolerances. Constraints make this problem depend on the geometry of the permitted solution set.

The proposed framework has a conditional guarantee: a quadratic program over that set must admit a polynomial-time rho-approximate solution, for a positive constant rho below one. Under this condition, it reaches an (epsilon, gamma)-second-order stationary point within O(max{epsilon^-2, rho^-3 gamma^-3}) iterations. The bound explicitly connects accuracy requirements and the quadratic approximation quality to the iteration count.

The authors also characterize overall complexity for sets described by quadratic constraints when the objective's Hessian has a specified structure over the set. They extend the analysis to stochastic optimization and count the stochastic gradient and Hessian evaluations needed. The contribution is therefore a framework whose guarantees follow from tractable quadratic subproblems, with further results for structured constraints and stochastic information.
neurips-2018-escaping-saddle-points-in-c.tldr: A constrained optimization framework reaches approximate second-order stationary points when suitable quadratic subproblems can be approximated efficiently.

paragraphs: This paper compares human object recognition with three convolutional networks under twelve kinds of image degradation. The networks are ResNet-152, VGG-19, and GoogLeNet. Humans are more robust to nearly all tested manipulations, and the patterns of classification errors increasingly differ between humans and networks as the visual signal becomes weaker.

Training networks directly on distorted images changes the comparison. They consistently exceed human performance on the exact distortion types included in training, but generalize extremely poorly to other types. The paper gives a concrete example: learning robustness to salt-and-pepper noise does not provide robustness to uniform white noise, and the reverse transfer also fails.

The findings separate success on familiar degradation from robustness when the noise distribution changes. That distinction makes variation between training and testing a central challenge for the evaluated vision systems. The authors point to lifelong machine learning as an approach for systematically addressing it. They also provide a dataset of 83,000 measured human psychophysical trials, offering a human reference for studying robustness to degraded images.
neurips-2018-generalisation-in-humans-an.tldr: Networks can surpass humans on trained image distortions yet transfer that robustness poorly to different distortion types.

paragraphs: Uniform stability describes how sensitive a learning algorithm is to changes in its training data. It can be used to bound generalization error, linking behavior on training samples to performance beyond them. The paper strengthens these guarantees for losses bounded between zero and one, without adding assumptions to the existing setting.

The previous high-probability bound becomes uninformative in many common settings where the stability parameter gamma is at least 1/sqrt(n). The authors prove a bound of O(sqrt((gamma + 1/n) log(1/delta))) with probability at least 1-delta. Here n is the sample count and delta controls the allowed failure probability. This improves the dependence on stability and sample size.

They also establish a tight O(gamma² + 1/n) bound on the second moment of generalization error, improving the previous O(gamma + 1/n) result. The second moment measures the expected squared error, complementing the high-probability guarantee. New analysis techniques yield both results, and the authors state that these improvements provide substantially stronger generalization guarantees for several well-studied algorithms.
neurips-2018-generalization-bounds-for-u.tldr: Stronger stability-based bounds improve high-probability and expected-squared generalization guarantees without additional assumptions.

paragraphs: The paper introduces interactive structure learning as a common framework for multiple interactive learning tasks. The emphasis is on learning through interaction within a shared formulation. Bringing these tasks together allows the authors to study an algorithmic approach and its behavior across the framework, rather than treating every task as a separate problem.

Within this setting, the authors generalize query-by-committee, an active learning algorithm. The resulting structural version connects the choice of learning queries to the broader structure-learning framework. This is the paper's algorithmic contribution: adapting an existing active learning approach so that it can be studied in the newly unified setting.

The analysis examines consistency and rate of convergence, asking whether learning approaches the intended result and how quickly it progresses. The authors investigate these questions both theoretically and empirically, considering settings with noise as well as without it. The stated contribution combines a unifying formulation, a generalized algorithm, and an assessment of its learning behavior across those feedback conditions.
neurips-2018-interactive-structure-learn.tldr: Interactive structure learning unifies several interactive tasks and extends query-by-committee with theoretical and empirical analysis under noisy and noiseless feedback.

paragraphs: IntroVAE combines reconstruction-based and adversarial training to generate high-resolution photographic images. Its inference model serves two purposes: it supports the latent representation used for reconstruction and helps assess whether samples are real or generated. This gives the model an internal mechanism for evaluating its own generated images during training.

The generator reconstructs input images from noisy inference outputs, following the variational autoencoder approach. At the same time, the inference model learns to distinguish real samples from generated ones, while the generator tries to fool it. Both objectives fit within a single-stream architecture trained in one stage, with no extra discriminator network required.

The authors report that IntroVAE retains VAE benefits including stable training and a well-behaved latent manifold. Experiments produce photorealistic images at high resolution, including 1024-by-1024 CelebA images, with results comparable to or better than state-of-the-art GANs. These findings support using the inference model itself as the adversarial evaluator while keeping reconstruction and image generation integrated in the same training framework.
neurips-2018-introvae-introspective-vari.tldr: IntroVAE uses its inference network as an adversarial evaluator to generate high-resolution photographic images without an extra discriminator.

paragraphs: The paper asks how a generative model can imagine a visual path from a system's current configuration to a desired goal. The intended output is a plausible sequence of observations that could later serve as a reference trajectory for control. High-dimensional inputs such as images make learning a useful planning representation central to this task.

The framework generates sequential observations from transitions in a low-dimensional planning model together with additional noise. It maximizes mutual information between those transitions and the generated observations, encouraging the representation to explain the data's causal dynamics. The planning model is structured for compatibility with efficient planning algorithms, with proposed versions using discrete or continuous states.

To produce a plan, the method maps current and goal observations into planning states, finds a trajectory between them, and converts that trajectory back into observations through the generator. The authors demonstrate plausible visual plans for rope manipulation. The result connects representation learning to an explicit planning process, making the learned representation useful for constructing goal-directed observation sequences.
neurips-2018-learning-plannable-represen.tldr: Causal InfoGAN learns compact planning states and renders planned trajectories as plausible visual sequences, demonstrated on rope manipulation.

paragraphs: Deep latent variable models combine neural networks with probabilistic generative modeling. Although variational methods commonly handle inference, this paper investigates the models' exact likelihood and its practical consequences. It focuses on two tasks where likelihood is central: estimating model parameters and filling in missing data.

The authors show that most unconstrained models used for continuous data have an unbounded likelihood. This means the likelihood can increase without reaching a finite maximum, making maximum likelihood estimation problematic. They demonstrate that this behavior can cause mode collapse. They also show how to ensure that maximum likelihood estimates exist and connect the analysis to nonparametric mixture models.

For missing-data imputation, the paper introduces an algorithm based on a model's exact conditional likelihood. Across several datasets, it consistently and significantly outperforms the usual imputation procedure used for these models. The findings give exact likelihood two practical roles: diagnosing a source of failure in parameter estimation and supporting improved reconstruction of missing values. The unboundedness result specifically concerns the unconstrained continuous-data models described by the authors.
neurips-2018-leveraging-the-exact-likeli.tldr: Studying exact likelihood reveals a source of mode collapse in deep latent models and yields an improved missing-data imputation method.

paragraphs: Standard mixed regression assumes that each response comes from one mixture component. This paper considers a broader setting where several components can contribute additively to the same response. That change allows the prediction model to represent combined contributions while retaining ordinary mixed regression as a special case.

The proposed estimator, MixLasso, uses a convex objective with an atomic norm designed to regularize the number of mixture components. This addresses difficulties associated with local-search approaches such as EM, which can encounter spurious local optima. The authors also contrast their approach with tensor-based methods that may need many samples or knowledge of the input distribution.

The analysis provides a risk bound balancing prediction accuracy against model sparsity without stringent assumptions on the input/output distribution. The method can also be adapted to nonlinear functions. Numerical experiments on both linear and nonlinear regression mixtures produce high-quality solutions across a wider range of settings than existing approaches. Together, these results support the estimator's combination of component control, convex formulation, and flexibility in the regression functions.
neurips-2018-mixlasso-generalized-mixed-.tldr: MixLasso uses convex atomic-norm regularization to estimate additive mixtures of regression components while balancing accuracy and sparsity.

paragraphs: The paper examines generative models trained by adversarially optimizing the kernel of Maximum Mean Discrepancy, or MMD. In this setting, the critic shapes the comparison used to train the generator. The authors show that controlling the critic's gradient is essential for obtaining a sensible loss function, making regularization a central design issue.

They introduce a principled method that enforces gradient constraints exactly through analytical means. Existing techniques discussed in the abstract instead use additive regularizers to approximate this control. The proposed constraints come at no additional cost relative to those approximate techniques, and the resulting loss function is provably continuous.

Experiments show more stable and faster training. The resulting image generators outperform state-of-the-art methods on CelebA at 160-by-160 resolution and unconditional ImageNet at 64-by-64 resolution. The contribution links a mathematical property of the training objective to observed optimization improvements and generation performance. Its exactness claim concerns the analytical gradient constraints, while the training and image-quality improvements are supported by the reported experiments.
neurips-2018-on-gradient-regularizers-fo.tldr: Exact analytical gradient constraints give MMD-based adversarial models a continuous loss and improve training and image generation in experiments.

paragraphs: The task is to translate a single image from one domain into an analogous image in another domain. Training provides only that one source image but a collection of target-domain images. The authors present empirical evidence that existing unsupervised translation methods fail in this setting, motivating a method designed around the uneven data availability.

Their approach has two stages. First, they train a variational autoencoder on the target-domain collection. After receiving the single source image, they construct a source-domain autoencoder by adapting the layers closest to the image to fit it directly. The remaining layers are adapted only indirectly, giving different parts of the network different adaptation roles.

Experiments indicate that this method, using one source sample, performs as well as existing domain-transfer methods supplied with many source-domain samples. The significance is the reduction in source examples needed for the reported comparisons. The target-domain collection remains part of the setup, so the one-shot claim specifically concerns the source side of the translation problem.
neurips-2018-one-shot-unsupervised-cross.tldr: A two-stage autoencoder method translates from a single source image using a target-domain image collection.

paragraphs: Generating a scene from text requires representing objects, visual concepts, and relationships among them. The paper frames this as a compositional generation problem: a model needs a process for assembling the scene, representations of the elements being assembled, and a way to turn abstract concepts into pixels.

PNP-Net addresses these requirements within a variational autoencoder framework. Its network structure is dynamic, allowing the image-composition process to vary. It also learns distribution transformers that combine probability distributions according to semantics. These transformers provide a probabilistic mechanism for composing the visual concepts involved in a scene.

The model then samples from the composed distributions and decodes those samples into realistic images. This connects semantic composition to pixel-level rendering through a single generative framework. The importance of the design is how its components correspond to the three requirements identified by the authors: organizing generation, composing visual elements, and rendering their realization. Its probabilistic representation also accommodates the variability that makes complicated scene generation challenging.
neurips-2018-probabilistic-neural-progra.tldr: PNP-Net generates scenes by dynamically composing semantic probability distributions and decoding samples into images.

paragraphs: This paper studies K-means clustering with additional information from queries asking whether two points belong to the same cluster. It also considers erroneous answers and outliers that belong to no cluster. The aim is to use such information efficiently while obtaining a clustering objective close to the optimum.

Under assumptions on the smallest cluster size, the method achieves a (1+epsilon)-approximation with probability at least 1-delta. In the noiseless setting, the expected query count is O(K³/(epsilon delta)), and comparison-based clustering takes O(ndK + K³/(epsilon delta)) operations. Compared with certain importance-sampling approaches, the query reduction is roughly a factor of O(K⁶/epsilon³), with the tradeoff that very small clusters may be missed.

The analysis estimates cluster sizes and the samples needed for accurate centroids, using generalizations of the double Dixie cup problem. Extensions address noisy query responses and outliers. Experiments on synthetic and real data, including MNIST and CIFAR-10, illustrate performance. The contribution connects query efficiency to explicit cluster-size conditions and a stated small-cluster tradeoff.
neurips-2018-query-k-means-clustering-an.tldr: Same-cluster queries enable efficient approximate K-means under cluster-size assumptions, with extensions for noisy answers and outliers.

paragraphs: Regularized empirical risk minimization trains a model by balancing fit to observed data with a regularization term. This paper considers that common learning objective for linear predictors. Its focus is the computational expense of optimization, especially when the prediction problem has many dimensions and repeated updates can become costly.

The authors propose a stochastic primal-dual method requiring O(1) operations per iteration. The central computational claim is therefore about the cost of an individual update. They also develop a variance-reduction variant with linear convergence, adding a convergence-rate result to the inexpensive-update design. These are complementary aspects of the method's optimization behavior.

Numerical experiments suggest that the proposed methods are faster than proximal SGD, SVRG, and SAGA on high-dimensional problems. That comparison provides empirical support for the approach's practical speed in the studied setting. The paper's contribution combines constant-cost iterations with a linearly convergent variant, while the reported experiments connect those algorithmic properties to observed runtime advantages for regularized linear prediction.
neurips-2018-stochastic-primal-dual-meth.tldr: A stochastic primal-dual optimizer uses constant-cost iterations, with a linearly convergent variance-reduction variant and promising high-dimensional runtime results.

paragraphs: Networks controlling agents in the physical world need timely responses and effective integration of information over time. This paper studies how a network is rolled out, meaning how its computations are arranged across time. Conventional sequential evaluation of layers can delay responses and produce sparse temporal integration.

The authors develop a theoretical framework describing different rollouts and the model parallelism they permit. They prove that certain arrangements allow earlier and more frequent responses, including for networks with skip connections but no recurrent connections. Experiments further show better performance for these early responses on the tasks studied, connecting computation timing to prediction usefulness.

The streaming rollout maximizes these response properties and allows fully parallel execution of the network, reducing runtime on massively parallel devices. The authors also provide an open-source toolbox for designing, training, evaluating, and interacting with streaming rollouts. The contribution makes temporal execution an explicit part of network design, linking formal response-time properties, empirical task behavior, and a route to exploiting parallel hardware.
neurips-2018-the-streaming-rollout-of-de.tldr: Streaming rollouts arrange network computation for earlier, more frequent responses and fully parallel execution on suitable hardware.

paragraphs: The paper presents an unsupervised way to discover and summarize artistic styles in large painting collections. It applies archetypal analysis to deep image representations, learning a dictionary of styles that can be visualized. This turns the collection into a set of interpretable reference styles for analyzing further images.

A new image's style is represented through local statistics of deep visual features. The method approximates those statistics with a sparse convex combination of learned archetypes. In plain terms, a small selection of archetypes contributes in nonnegative proportions that sum to one. The decomposition indicates which reference styles are present and their relative contributions.

Those same proportions become controls for manipulating style. Changing the coefficients enables effects including enhancement, transfer, and interpolation among multiple archetypes. The significance is that discovery, interpretation, and manipulation share one representation: the learned dictionary explains an image and supplies the ingredients for altering it. The method connects a geometric form of unsupervised learning to visual effects through an explicit, editable decomposition.
neurips-2018-unsupervised-learning-of-ar.tldr: Archetypal style analysis learns interpretable artistic styles and represents images as editable mixtures of those styles.
